items.label: Setup S-1
items.nl: An original record is \(O=(X,A,Y)\in[0,1]\times\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R\), and an original law \(P\) is a Borel probability measure on that space with covariate marginal \(P_X\). Let \(\lambda\) be Lebesgue measure on \([0,1]\) and, for \(0<s\le1\), let \(\mathcal H^s(20)\) be the continuous functions on \([0,1]\) with sup norm and \(s\)-H\"older constant at most \(20\). For a Borel \(f\), \([f]_\lambda\) is its \(\lambda\)-almost-everywhere class and \(\operatorname{rep}\) selects the unique continuous member of a class when one exists. The propensity class is \(\mathcal E_P=[x\mapsto P(A=1\mid X=x)]_\lambda\), the arm kernels are \(Q_{a,P}(dy\mid x)\), the arm-mean classes are \(\mathcal G_{a,P}=[x\mapsto\int y\,Q_{a,P}(dy\mid x)]_\lambda\), and \(e_P,m_{0,P},m_{1,P}\) are their continuous representatives, with \(\tau_P=m_{1,P}-m_{0,P}\), \(\bar\tau_P=\int_0^1\tau_P\,d\lambda\) and \(d(P)=\{\int_0^1(\tau_P-\bar\tau_P)^2\,d\lambda\}^{1/2}\). For a public tuple \(v=(p,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in\mathcal V=(1,2]\times(0,1]\times(0,1]\times[1/4,1]\), the class \(\mathcal M_v\) consists of the laws with \(P_X=\lambda\), \(e_P\in\mathcal H^\alpha(20)\) with range in \([1/4,3/4]\), \(m_{0,P}\in\mathcal H^\beta(20)\), \(\tau_P\in\mathcal H^\gamma(20)\), \(\|m_{0,P}\|_\infty\le1/2\), \(\|\tau_P\|_\infty\le1/2\) and \(\max_a\operatorname{ess\,sup}_{x}\int|y|^p\,Q_{a,P}(dy\mid x)\le10\). The null \(H_0(v)\) is the subclass on which \(\tau_P\equiv c\) for some \(c\in[-1/2,1/2]\). For \(w=(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in\mathcal W=(0,1]\times(0,1]\times[1/4,1]\), \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm b}_w\) and \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{bin}}_w\) are the members of \(\mathcal M_{(2,w)}\) with \(P(|Y|\le1)=1\), respectively \(P(Y\in\{-1,1\})=1\), with nulls \(H_0^{\mathrm b}(w)\), \(H_0^{\mathrm{bin}}(w)\); \(D_v,D^{\mathrm b}_w,D^{\mathrm{bin}}_w\) are the suprema of \(d\) over the three classes and \(d_0=1/(8\sqrt2)\). The broader supplied-propensity class \(\mathcal M_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}\) keeps the continuous representatives \(e_P,m_{0,P},m_{1,P}\) and every condition of \(\mathcal M_v\) except the two quantitative requirements \(e_P\in\mathcal H^\alpha(20)\) and \(m_{0,P}\in\mathcal H^\beta(20)\); its null \(H_0^{\mathrm{e,br}}(v)\) is the subclass with \(\tau_P\equiv c\) for some \(c\in[-1/2,1/2]\), and \(D_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}=\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}}d(P)\). The data are \(\mathcal D_n=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\sim P^{\otimes n}\) with \(n\ge2\), together with an independent \(U\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\). The causal completion \(\mathbb Q_P\) draws \(X\sim\lambda\), then \(Y(0)\sim Q_{0,P}(\cdot\mid X)\), \(Y(1)\sim Q_{1,P}(\cdot\mid X)\) and \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(e_P(X))\) conditionally independently, and sets \(Y=(1-A)Y(0)+AY(1)\).

items.label: Setup S-2
items.nl: A randomized original-record test is a jointly Borel map \(\phi:([0,1]\times\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R)^n\times[0,1]\to[0,1]\) with rejection expectation \(\mathsf R_n(P,\phi)=\int\phi(\mathcal D_n,u)\,P^{\otimes n}(d\mathcal D_n)\,du\). For a separation \(r\in(0,D_v)\), \(B_n(v,r)\) is the infimum, over tests with \(\sup_{P\in H_0(v)}\mathsf R_n(P,\phi)\le1/10\), of \(\sup\{1-\mathsf R_n(P,\phi):P\in\mathcal M_v,\ d(P)\ge r\}\), and the capped critical radius is \(r_n^*(v)=\inf(\{r\in(0,D_v):B_n(v,r)\le1/10\}\cup\{D_v\})\). The bounded and signed-binary risks \(B_n^{\mathrm b},B_n^{\mathrm{bin}}\) and radii \(r_n^{*,\mathrm b},r_n^{*,\mathrm{bin}}\) are defined identically over \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm b}_w\), \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{bin}}_w\) and their nulls. In the supplied-propensity experiment a test \(\phi^{\mathrm e}\) is a Borel map on \(C([0,1])\times([0,1]\times\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R)^n\times[0,1]\) (uniform topology on the first factor) evaluated at \(e_P\), with expectation \(\mathsf R_n^{\mathrm e}\), risk \(B_n^{\mathrm e}\) and radius \(r_n^{*,\mathrm e}\) over the same class \(\mathcal M_v\). With the same tests and the same expectation \(\mathsf R_n^{\mathrm e}\), the broader-class risk \(B_n^{\mathrm{e,br}}(v,r)\), for \(0<r<D_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}\), is the infimum over tests with \(\sup_{P\in H_0^{\mathrm{e,br}}(v)}\mathsf R_n^{\mathrm e}(P,\phi^{\mathrm e})\le1/10\) of \(\sup\{1-\mathsf R_n^{\mathrm e}(P,\phi^{\mathrm e}):P\in\mathcal M_v^{\mathrm{e,br}},\ d(P)\ge r\}\), and \(r_n^{*,\mathrm{e,br}}(v)=\inf(\{r\in(0,D_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}):B_n^{\mathrm{e,br}}(v,r)\le1/10\}\cup\{D_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}\})\). The radius ratio is \(\Delta_n(v)=r_n^*(v)/r_n^{*,\mathrm b}(w)\); \(\mathcal T=\{v\in\mathcal V:p<2,\ \Delta_n(v)\to\infty\}\), \(\mathcal E=\{v\in\mathcal V:\sup_{n\ge2}\Delta_n(v)<\infty\}\) and \(\mathcal R=\{v\in\mathcal V:\sup_{n\ge2}r_n^*(v)/r_n^{*,\mathrm e}(v)<\infty\}\). Total variation is \(\operatorname{TV}(\mu,\nu)=\sup_B|\mu(B)-\nu(B)|\).

items.label: Setup S-3
items.nl: For \(v=(p,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in\mathcal V\) put \(q=(p-1)/p\), \(S=\alpha+\beta\), \(D_p=1+2\alpha+\beta/q+S/(2\gamma)\), \(E_0(p)=2\gamma q/(2\gamma+q)\), \(E_4(p)=2S/D_p\), \(F(p)=2\alpha/(p-1)+\beta/q+S/(2\gamma)\) and \(E(p)=\min\{E_0(p),E_4(p)\}\). The explicit scales are \(\rho_n(v)=n^{-E(p)}\), \(\rho_n^{\mathrm b}(w)=n^{-E(2)}\) and \(\rho_n^{\mathrm e}(v)=n^{-E_0(p)}\). With \(H_{\mathrm{fine}}=2^{40}\), \(N_{\mathrm{low}}(v)=\lceil\max\{2,32^{D_p\gamma/(2S)}\}\rceil\), \(k_v=2^{-17}(2H_{\mathrm{fine}})^{-S}\) and \(c_0^{\mathrm e}=4^{-\gamma}/(16\sqrt3)\), the lower multiplier is \(c_v=c_0^{\mathrm e}\) if \(F(p)\ge1\) and \(c_v=\min\{k_v,c_0^{\mathrm e}N_{\mathrm{low}}(v)^{-(E_0(p)-E_4(p))}\}\) otherwise, and \(c^{\mathrm b}_w=c_{(2,w)}\). The attainment multiplier \(C_v\) and threshold \(N_v=\lceil\max\{4,(2C_v/d_0)^{1/E(p)}\}\rceil\) are explicit public functions of \(v\), with \(C^{\mathrm b}_w=C_{(2,w)}\), \(N^{\mathrm b}_w=N_{(2,w)}\). The rules \(\phi^*_{n,v}\), \(\phi^{*,\mathrm b}_{n,w}=\phi^*_{n,(2,w)}\) and the supplied-propensity rule \(\phi^{*,\mathrm e}_{n,v}\) are explicit measurable functions of the records; the profiling constant is \(C=128\).

items.label: Setup S-4
items.nl: For a positive integer rank \(J\), the cells are \(I_{j,J}=[(j-1)/J,j/J)\) for \(j<J\) and \(I_{J,J}=[(J-1)/J,1]\), the feature map is \(F_J(x)=(\sqrt J\,\mathbf 1_{I_{j,J}}(x))_{j=1}^J\), the histogram kernel is \(\Pi_J(x,z)=\langle F_J(x),F_J(z)\rangle\) and \((\Pi_Jf)(x)=\int_0^1\Pi_J(x,z)f(z)\,dz\). The coarse and fine ranks \(J_{\mathrm c}\le J_{\mathrm f}\) are powers of two, \(T\ge1\) is a clipping level with \(\ell_T(y)=\max\{-T,\min\{y,T\}\}\), \(s_n=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), and the evaluation blocks are \(\mathcal I_1=\{1,\ldots,s_n\}\), \(\mathcal I_2=\{s_n+1,\ldots,2s_n\}\). For a kernel \(G:[0,1]^2\to\mathbb R\) and \(c\in[-1/2,1/2]\), the block scores are \(H_{b,T}(c)=s_n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_b}F_{J_{\mathrm c}}(X_i)A_i\{\ell_T(Y_i)-c\}\) and \(U_{b,G,T}(c)=\{s_n(s_n-1)\}^{-1}\sum_{i\ne j\in\mathcal I_b}F_{J_{\mathrm c}}(X_i)A_iG(X_i,X_j)\{\ell_T(Y_j)-cA_j\}\) for \(n\ge4\) and zero for \(n=2,3\). The multiresolution score \(Z_b(c)\) subtracts from \(H_{b,T_0}(c)\) an initial correction and nested dyadic increments with level-specific cutoffs, \(\theta_P(c)=E_PZ_b(c)\), \(W(c)=\langle Z_1(c),Z_2(c)\rangle\), and \(\mathfrak b_{n,v}\), \(\Lambda_{n,v}\), \(h_{n,v}\) are the public bias ledger, covariance ledger and rejection cutoff; the rule rejects when \(\min_{|c|\le1/2}W(c)>h_{n,v}\).

items.label: Setup S-5
Definition P-1
items.nl: \(\mathcal M_v=\{P:\ P_X=\lambda,\ \max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{x\sim\lambda}\int |y|^pQ_{a,P}(dy\mid x)\le10,\ \exists f\in\mathcal H^\alpha(20),\ g_0\in\mathcal H^\beta(20),\ g_1\in C([0,1]):\ \mathcal E_P=[f]_\lambda,\ \mathcal G_{0,P}=[g_0]_\lambda,\ \mathcal G_{1,P}=[g_1]_\lambda,\ f([0,1])\subseteq[1/4,3/4],\ g_1-g_0\in\mathcal H^\gamma(20),\ \|g_0\|_\infty\le1/2,\ \|g_1-g_0\|_\infty\le1/2\},\quad v=(p,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in\mathcal V\). The continuous representatives in this membership predicate are \(e_P,m_{0,P},m_{1,P}\); the effect is their canonical difference \(\tau_P\).

items.label: Definition P-2
items.nl: \(\mathbb Q_P(dx,dy_0,dy_1,da)=\lambda(dx)Q_{0,P}(dy_0\mid x)Q_{1,P}(dy_1\mid x)e_P(x)^a(1-e_P(x))^{1-a},\quad Y=(1-A)Y(0)+AY(1)\). Kernel changes on \(\lambda\)-null sets leave \(\mathbb Q_P\) unchanged.

items.label: Definition P-8
items.nl: \(B_n^{\mathrm b}(w,r)=\inf_{\phi:\sup_{P\in H_0^{\mathrm b}(w)}\mathsf R_n(P,\phi)\le1/10}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm b}_w:d(P)\ge r}\{1-\mathsf R_n(P,\phi)\},\quad n\ge2,\ w\in\mathcal W,\ 0<r<D_w^{\mathrm b}\).

items.label: Definition P-9
items.nl: \(B_n^{\mathrm{bin}}(w,r)=\inf_{\phi:\sup_{P\in H_0^{\mathrm{bin}}(w)}\mathsf R_n(P,\phi)\le1/10}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm{bin}}_w:d(P)\ge r}\{1-\mathsf R_n(P,\phi)\},\quad n\ge2,\ w\in\mathcal W,\ 0<r<D_w^{\mathrm{bin}}\).

items.label: Definition P-14
items.nl: The defined object is exactly the capped-radius ratio \[\Delta_n(v)=\frac{r_n^*(v)}{r_n^{*,\mathrm b}(w)},\qquad w=(\alpha,\beta,\gamma).\] Both numerator and denominator are the capped critical radii of the original-record experiments in Definition \(\mathrm{def:testing\mbox{-}risk}\) and its bounded analogue, at the same sample size and matched smoothness tuple.

items.label: Definition P-15
items.nl: \(B_n(v,r)=\inf_{\phi:\ \sup_{P\in H_0(v)}\mathsf R_n(P,\phi)\le1/10}\ \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_v:\ d(P)\ge r}\{1-\mathsf R_n(P,\phi)\},\quad n\ge2,\ v\in\mathcal V,\ 0<r<D_v\).

items.label: Definition P-17
items.nl: \(B_n^{\mathrm e}(v,r)=\inf_{\phi^{\mathrm e}:\ \sup_{P\in H_0(v)}\mathsf R_n^{\mathrm e}(P,\phi^{\mathrm e})\le1/10}\ \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_v:\ d(P)\ge r}\{1-\mathsf R_n^{\mathrm e}(P,\phi^{\mathrm e})\},\quad n\ge2,\ v\in\mathcal V,\ 0<r<D_v\).

items.label: Definition P-20
items.nl: \(I_{j,J}=[(j-1)/J,j/J)\) for \(j<J\), with \(I_{J,J}=[(J-1)/J,1]\); \(F_J(x)=(\sqrt J\,\mathbf1_{I_{j,J}}(x))_{j=1}^J\), \(\Pi_J(x,z)=\langle F_J(x),F_J(z)\rangle\), and \((\Pi_J f)(x)=\int_0^1\Pi_J(x,z)f(z)\,dz\).

items.label: Definition P-22
items.nl: For \(n\ge4\), \[H_{b,T}(c)=s_n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_b}F_{J_{\mathrm c}}(X_i)A_i\{\ell_T(Y_i)-c\},\qquad U_{b,G,T}(c)=\{s_n(s_n-1)\}^{-1}\sum_{i\ne j\in\mathcal I_b}F_{J_{\mathrm c}}(X_i)A_iG(X_i,X_j)\{\ell_T(Y_j)-cA_j\}.\] Set both vectors to zero for \(n=2,3\).

items.label: Definition P-23
items.nl: This handle is the branchwise score, ledger, profiling operation and rejection rule specified in Definition \(\mathrm{def:explicit\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}ledger}\). In its multiresolution branch, with \(M=J_{\mathrm c}\), \(K=J_{\mathrm f}\), \(R_j=2^jM\), \(D_j=\Pi_{R_j}-\Pi_{R_{j-1}}\), main cutoff \(T_0\), and separately selected increment cutoffs \(T_j\), define exactly \[Z_b(c)=H_{b,T_0}(c)-U_{b,\Pi_M,T_0}(c)-\sum_{j=1}^{\log_2(K/M)}U_{b,D_j,T_j}(c).\] In the single-correction branch define exactly \(Z_b(c)=H_{b,T_0}(c)-U_{b,\Pi_K,T_0}(c)\). In either branch use the affine convention \(Z_b(c)=Z_{b,0}-cZ_{b,A}\), where \(Z_{b,0}=Z_b(0)\) and \(Z_{b,A}=Z_b(0)-Z_b(1)\). The dyadic ranks and cutoffs, the deterministic original-mean bias ledger \(\mathfrak b_{n,v}=B\), the covariance ledger \(\Lambda_{n,v}=L_1^2/s+2L_2^2/[s(s-1)]\) bounding both affine-coefficient variances and their cross-covariance, and the upper-dyadic rejection cutoff \(h_{n,v}=\mathcal R(2B^2+2^{16}\sqrt M\Lambda_{n,v})\) are exactly the finite public selections in that definition. Put \(W(c)=\langle Z_1(c),Z_2(c)\rangle\), compute its minimum on \([-1/2,1/2]\) from the two endpoints and, only when present, its positive-curvature interior vertex, and reject exactly when this minimum exceeds \(h_{n,v}\). Use the zero rule at \(n=2,3\).

items.label: Definition P-24
items.nl: Use exactly the two score members of Definition \(\mathrm{def:calibration\mbox{-}handle}\). For the multiresolution member take coarse rank \(J_{\mathrm c}=J\), fine rank \(J_{\mathrm f}=2^LJ\), main cutoff \(T_0\), and increment cutoffs \(T_j\), \(j\in\operatorname{Fin}(L)\); for the single-correction member take coarse rank \(J_{\mathrm c}=J\), fine rank \(J_{\mathrm f}=K\), and cutoff \(T_0\). In either branch compute the population original mean \[\int_0^1F_{J_{\mathrm c}}(x)\{e_P(x)(1-(\Pi_{J_{\mathrm f}}e_P)(x))(\tau_P(x)-c)+(e_P(x)-(\Pi_{J_{\mathrm f}}e_P)(x))m_{0,P}(x)\}\,dx,\] and add respectively the exact multiresolution or single-correction clipping-tail remainder. For each affine coefficient \(r\in\{0,1\}\), let \(h_r\) be the branch's raw single-record kernel and \(g_r\) its raw symmetric pair kernel. Retain their population coefficient means \(\mathbb E h_r+\mathbb E g_r\), singleton projections \(h_r-\mathbb E h_r+2g_{r,1}\), and canonical pair projections \(g_r-\mathbb E g_r-g_{r,1}(o)-g_{r,1}(z)\). For every pair \(r,r'\), retain the four population raw-kernel contractions \(h_r\!\times h_{r'}\), \(h_r\!\times g_{r'}\), \(g_r\!\times h_{r'}\), and \(g_r\!\times g_{r'}\), where each contraction is the expectation of a Euclidean inner product over the displayed independent records. For each \(c\), put \(h_c=h_0-c h_1\) and \(g_c=g_0-c g_1\). The sample object is the single \(c\)-indexed normalized two-block statistic \(W(c)=\langle Z_0(c),Z_1(c)\rangle\), expanded as the total of its two-, three-, and four-record sums of Euclidean inner products over independent blocks and distinct within-block indices. Its two mixed affine-coefficient contributions are retained through their sum, rather than as separate sample outputs.

items.label: Definition P-25
items.nl: \[\begin{aligned}\mathsf T\bigl(A=(1+\ell)/2,Y=hL\mid X=x\bigr)&=\frac{\varepsilon}{4}(1+\ell\xi+h\upsilon+\ell h\zeta),\\ \mathsf T\bigl(A=(1+\ell)/2,Y=0\mid X=x\bigr)&=\frac{1-\varepsilon}{2}(1+\ell\xi),\qquad (\ell,h)\in\{-1,1\}^2.\end{aligned}\] Inputs \(\xi,\upsilon,\zeta\) may be Borel functions of the covariate; this table is evaluated on inputs making its displayed probabilities nonnegative. Retain all six record categories in likelihood products.

items.label: Definition P-26
items.nl: This definition names only the finite-overlap frame and its coefficient fields. For \(K=J_{\mathrm f}\), define \(f_i(x)=\cos(\pi(Kx-i)/2)\) on \([i/K,(i+1)/K]\), define \(f_i(x)=\sin(\pi(Kx-(i-1))/2)\) on \([(i-1)/K,i/K]\) when \(i>0\), and set it to zero elsewhere. For a coefficient vector \(a=(a_0,\ldots,a_K)\), its frame field is \(x\mapsto\sum_{i=0}^K a_if_i(x)\). The copula coupling, opposite coarse tents, normalized marked tables and mixture integration are separate operations defined in Definition \(\mathrm{def:copula\mbox{-}frame\mbox{-}priors}\); they are not part of the frame object.

items.label: Definition P-27
items.nl: Select the following explicit branchwise finite priors. If \(F(p)<1\) and \(n\ge N_{\mathrm{low}}(v)\), let \(K\) be the least power of two at least \(H_{\mathrm{fine}}n^{2/D_p}\), let \(M=2^{\lfloor\log_2(K^{(\alpha+\beta)/\gamma}/16)\rfloor}\), and use the priors of Definition \(\mathrm{def:copula\mbox{-}frame\mbox{-}priors}\) with \(a=K^{-\alpha}/16\), \(u=1/16\), \(\varepsilon_{n,v}=16^{-1/q}K^{-\beta/q}\), and \(L_{n,v}=\varepsilon_{n,v}^{-1/p}\). Otherwise use the established opposite paired-tent null and alternative priors with \(N=2\lceil n^{2q/(2\gamma+q)}\rceil\), \(h=1/N\), \(\varepsilon_{n,v}=h^{\gamma/q}\), and \(L_{n,v}=h^{-\gamma/(p-1)}\). Denote the selected null and alternative priors by \(\pi_{0,n,v}\) and \(\pi_{1,n,v}\), and their complete iid record mixtures by \(\mathbb P_{0,n,v}\) and \(\mathbb P_{1,n,v}\). The stated balancing, support-law legality, true null-mixture denominator, complete occupancy and transition accounting, and bounded-scale comparison are the stipulated properties of this selected construction.

items.label: Definition P-28
items.nl: For \(n\ge2\), put \(s=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), \(q=(p-1)/p\), \(E_0=2\gamma q/(2\gamma+q)\), and \(a=s^{-E_0}\). Let \(T=2^{\lceil\log_2(a^{-1/(p-1)})\rceil}\) and let \(J\) be the least power of two at least \(a^{-1/\gamma}\). Put \(\widetilde e=\max\{1/4,\min\{e,3/4\}\}\); for every legal supplied true propensity, \(\widetilde e=e\). Form the clipped original inverse-propensity score \(R_i=A_i\ell_T(Y_i)/\widetilde e(X_i)-(1-A_i)\ell_T(Y_i)/(1-\widetilde e(X_i))\), and let \(V_b=s^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_b}(\Pi_J-1)R_i\), equivalently the centered histogram-feature vector in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:oracle\mbox{-}frontier\mbox{-}resolved}\). Define \(b=20T^{1-p}\) and \(\Lambda=80T^{2-p}/s\), and reject exactly when \(\langle V_1,V_2\rangle>2b^2+1024\sqrt J\Lambda\). This dyadic rate-balancing selection and threshold, rather than an unspecified optimization, define the supplied-propensity test. Its singleton and canonical quadratic projections, and the normalized common-propensity paired-tent converse, are the proved calibration and necessity properties used to compare its explicit scale with the unknown-propensity frontier.

items.label: Definition P-29
items.nl: For the original-record experiment, define \(\mathsf S_{n,P}=P^{\otimes n}\otimes\lambda\) on \( ([0,1]\times\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R)^n\times[0,1]\). The first coordinate is \(\mathcal D_n\), and the last is \(U\). Its test expectation is exactly the already stipulated \(\mathsf R_n(P,\phi)=\int\phi(\mathcal D_n,u)\,\mathsf S_{n,P}(d\mathcal D_n,du)\). Thus this definition names the given iid experiment and independent public randomization; it changes no member-law predicate.

items.label: Definition P-30
items.nl:
This is a specified member of Definition \(\mathrm{def:calibration\mbox{-}handle}\), constructed from the original records only. For the public tuple put
\[
 q=\frac{p-1}{p},\quad S=\alpha+\beta,\quad
 t=\frac{2-p}{p-1},\quad
 E_0=\frac{2\gamma q}{2\gamma+q},\quad
 E_4=\frac{2S}{1+2\alpha+\beta/q+S/(2\gamma)},\quad E=\min\{E_0,E_4\}.
\]
For \(n=2,3\), set \(J_{\mathrm c}=J_{\mathrm f}=1\), all cutoffs equal to one, \(Z_b(c)=0\), \(\mathfrak b_{n,v}=\Lambda_{n,v}=h_{n,v}=0\), and the rejection rule equal to zero. For \(n\ge4\), let \(s=s_n\), \(a=s^{-E}\), and let \(M=J_{\mathrm c}\) be the least power of two at least \(a^{-1/\gamma}\). Let \(K=J_{\mathrm f}\) be the least power of two at least \(\max\{M,a^{-1/S}\}\). For \(x>0\) put \(\mathcal R(x)=2^{\lceil\log_2 x\rceil}\). Put \(T_0=\mathcal R(a^{-1/(p-1)})\) and \(V_0=32T_0^{2-p}\).

If \(S\ge\gamma\) or \(\alpha\ge q\), define
\[
 Z_b(c)=H_{b,T_0}(c)-U_{b,\Pi_K,T_0}(c),\quad
 B=400K^{-S}+20T_0^{1-p},\quad
 L_1=16\sqrt{V_0},\quad L_2=4\sqrt{KV_0}.
\]
Otherwise let \(\lambda_0=(p-1)^2/(4p)\), \(L=\log_2(K/M)\), \(R_j=2^jM\), \(D_j=\Pi_{R_j}-\Pi_{R_{j-1}}\), and
\[
 T_j=\mathcal R\left(\max\left\{1,\min\left\{a^{-1/(p-1)},
 \left[\frac{R_j^{-\alpha}}{a(R_j/K)^{\lambda_0}}\right]^{1/(p-1)}\right\}\right\}\right),
 \qquad 1\le j\le L.
\]
For each defined increment cutoff set \(V_j=32T_j^{2-p}\). Here \(L\) is an integer and an empty sum has value zero. In this branch set
\[
 \begin{split}
 Z_b(c)&=H_{b,T_0}(c)-U_{b,\Pi_M,T_0}(c)
                 -\sum_{j=1}^L U_{b,D_j,T_j}(c),\\
 a_j&=40R_{j-1}^{-\alpha},\quad
 d_j=110R_{j-1}^{-\min\{\alpha,\beta,\gamma\}}+20T_j^{1-p},\\
 B&=400K^{-S}+20T_0^{1-p}+10\sum_{j=1}^L a_jT_j^{1-p},\\
 L_1&=16\sqrt{V_0}+8\sum_{j=1}^L(d_j+a_j\sqrt{V_j}),\\
 L_2&=4\left(\sqrt{MV_0}+\sum_{j=1}^L\sqrt{R_jV_j}\right).
 \end{split}
\]
In both branches define the public numbers
\[
 \mathfrak b_{n,v}=B,\quad
 \Lambda_{n,v}=\frac{L_1^2}{s}+\frac{2L_2^2}{s(s-1)},\quad
 h_{n,v}=\mathcal R(2B^2+2^{16}\sqrt M\Lambda_{n,v}).
\]
Use \(W(c)=\langle Z_1(c),Z_2(c)\rangle\) and reject exactly when \(\min_{|c|\le1/2}W(c)>h_{n,v}\). Compute this minimum from the two endpoints and, only for a positive quadratic coefficient and an interior vertex, the vertex. For public grid bookkeeping use the rank grid \(\{2^j:0\le j\le\lceil\log_2(2s^2)\rceil\}\) and the outcome grid \(\{2^j:0\le j\le\lceil\log_2(2s)\rceil\}\). The cutoff is the upper endpoint of the public two-point dyadic grid bracketing its unrounded formula. Every sum is finite. The definitions of the histogram and ordered-pair scores supply the values at bin endpoints, and there is no division by an observed cell count.

items.label: Definition P-31
items.nl:
Inputs are \(v\), dyadic integers \(K=J_{\mathrm f}\), \(M=J_{\mathrm c}\ge2\) with \(K\ge16M\), amplitudes \(0<a,u\le1/16\), and \(0<\varepsilon<1\), \(L>0\). Put \(\kappa=1/16\), and let \(b_\triangle(t)=2\min(t,1-t)\) on \([0,1]\). For independent uniform signs \(\sigma_j\), \(1\le j\le M/2\), define \(g_\sigma\) to be \(\sigma_j b_\triangle\) rescaled onto coarse cell \(2j-1\), and its negative rescaled onto cell \(2j\), with zero at cell boundaries. Let \(f_i\), \(0\le i\le K\), be the continuous frame: on \([i/K,(i+1)/K]\) its two nonzero coordinates are \(f_i(x)=\cos(\pi(Kx-i)/2)\), \(f_{i+1}(x)=\sin(\pi(Kx-i)/2)\). Put
\[
 \widetilde g_\sigma(x)=\sum_{i=0}^K g_\sigma(i/K)f_i(x)^2.
\]
For \(\nu=0,1\), conditionally on \(\sigma\), independently draw coefficient pairs with
\[
 \Pr_\nu(\lambda_i=l,\eta_i=h\mid\sigma)
 =\frac{1+\nu\kappa g_\sigma(i/K)lh}{4},\qquad l,h\in\{-1,1\}.
\]
For each draw name a record law by uniform \(X\) and the normalized table in Definition \(\mathrm{def:marked\mbox{-}table}\), using
\[
 \xi(x)=a\sum_i f_i(x)\lambda_i,\quad
 \upsilon(x)=u\sum_i f_i(x)\eta_i,\quad
 t_\nu(x)=-\frac{\nu a u\kappa}{1-a^2}\widetilde g_\sigma(x),\quad
 \zeta(x)=\xi(x)\upsilon(x)+t_\nu(x)(1-\xi(x)^2).
\]
The pushforward of these finite coefficient draws is \(\pi^{K,M}_{\nu;v,a,u,\varepsilon,L}\). This definition names tables and mixing laws; normalization, model membership, separation and mixture-distance properties are proved in the consuming lemmas.

items.label: Definition P-32
items.nl:
For \(v\in\mathcal V\), put
\[
 q=(p-1)/p,\quad S=\alpha+\beta,\quad
 D_p=1+2\alpha+\beta/q+S/(2\gamma),\quad
 E_0(p)=\frac{2\gamma q}{2\gamma+q},\quad E_4(p)=\frac{2S}{D_p},
 \quad F(p)=\frac{2\alpha}{p-1}+\frac\beta q+\frac S{2\gamma},
 \quad E(p)=\min\{E_0(p),E_4(p)\}.
\]
Here arguments \(p\) in \(E_0,E_4,F,E\) retain the same \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\). Define
\[
 H_{\mathrm{fine}}=2^{40},\quad
 N_{\mathrm{low}}(v)=\left\lceil\max\{2,32^{D_p\gamma/(2S)}\}\right\rceil,
 \quad k_v=2^{-17}(2H_{\mathrm{fine}})^{-S},\quad
 c_0^{\mathrm e}=4^{-\gamma}/(16\sqrt3).
\]
The sharp scales and lower multipliers are
\[
 \rho_n(v)=n^{-E(p)},\qquad \rho_n^{\mathrm b}(w)=n^{-E(2)},\qquad
 c_v=\begin{cases}
 c_0^{\mathrm e},&F(p)\ge1,\\
 \min\{k_v,c_0^{\mathrm e}N_{\mathrm{low}}(v)^{-(E_0(p)-E_4(p))}\},&F(p)<1,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad c_w^{\mathrm b}=c_{(2,w)}.
\]
Take \(C_v=C^{\mathrm{att}}_v\), \(N_v=N^{\mathrm{att}}_v\) with the fully evaluable formulas of Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:original\mbox{-}record\mbox{-}attainable\mbox{-}rate}\); take \(C_w^{\mathrm b}=C^{\mathrm{att}}_{(2,w)}\), \(N_w^{\mathrm b}=N^{\mathrm{att}}_{(2,w)}\). The rule \(\phi^*_{n,v}\) is exactly the total original-record rule of Definition \(\mathrm{def:explicit\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}ledger}\); \(\phi^{*,\mathrm b}_{n,w}\) is the same rule at tuple \((2,w)\). These definitions name scales and rules; their sharpness is a conclusion of the full-record lower and attainment proofs.

items.label: Definition P-33
items.nl:
For \(v=(p,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in\mathcal V\), define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathcal M_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}=\bigl\{P:\;&P_X=\lambda,\quad
 \max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{x\sim\lambda}
      \int |y|^p Q_{a,P}(dy\mid x)\le10,\\
&\exists f,g_0,g_1\in C([0,1]):\quad
 \mathcal E_P=[f]_\lambda,\quad
 \mathcal G_{0,P}=[g_0]_\lambda,\quad
 \mathcal G_{1,P}=[g_1]_\lambda,\\
&f([0,1])\subseteq[1/4,3/4],\quad
 g_1-g_0\in\mathcal H^\gamma(20),\quad
 \|g_0\|_\infty\le1/2,\quad \|g_1-g_0\|_\infty\le1/2
 \bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
The representatives are the existing functionals \(e_P,m_{0,P},m_{1,P}\), and \(\tau_P=m_{1,P}-m_{0,P}\). All three nuisance representatives retain their existing continuous carrier. Membership deletes exactly the quantitative \(\alpha\)-H\"older restriction on the propensity and the quantitative \(\beta\)-H\"older restriction on the baseline from Definition \(\mathrm{def:model}\). It retains the six listed member properties. The label \(v\) retains the existing public tuple for compatibility; this broader membership predicate depends only on \(p\) and \(\gamma\). Define its maximum distance by
\[
 D_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}=\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}}d(P).
\]
This definition introduces no observation carrier, supplied object or sampling experiment.

items.label: Definition P-34
items.nl:
Define
\[
 H_0^{\mathrm{e,br}}(v)=
 \left\{P\in\mathcal M_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}:
   \exists c\in[-1/2,1/2]\ \forall x\in[0,1],\ \tau_P(x)=c\right\}.
\]
The null adds the existing unknown-constant effect condition to the broader oracle model.

items.label: Definition P-35
items.nl:
For \(n\ge2\), \(v\in\mathcal V\) and \(0<r<D_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}\), define
\[
 B_n^{\mathrm{e,br}}(v,r)=
 \inf_{\phi^{\mathrm e}:\,
     \sup_{P\in H_0^{\mathrm{e,br}}(v)}
           \mathsf R_n^{\mathrm e}(P,\phi^{\mathrm e})\le1/10}
 \ \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}:\,d(P)\ge r}
           \{1-\mathsf R_n^{\mathrm e}(P,\phi^{\mathrm e})\}.
\]
The admissible \(\phi^{\mathrm e}\) are precisely the existing jointly Borel supplied-continuous-function tests with values in \([0,1]\). The expectation is the unchanged
\[
 \mathsf R_n^{\mathrm e}(P,\phi^{\mathrm e})
  =\int \phi^{\mathrm e}(e_P,\mathcal D_n,u)
                 \,P^{\otimes n}(d\mathcal D_n)\,du.
\]
Thus the experiment is the existing original iid sample and independent public uniform randomization, with the same whole true continuous propensity supplied as before.

items.label: Definition P-36
items.nl:
Define
\[
 r_n^{*,\mathrm{e,br}}(v)=
 \inf\left(
   \{r\in(0,D_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}):B_n^{\mathrm{e,br}}(v,r)\le1/10\}
        \cup\{D_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}\}\right).
\]
The model maximum is a saturation sentinel, with the same convention as the existing capped radius.

items.label: Lemma L-1
items.nl: For every \(v\in\mathcal V\) and \(P\in\mathcal M_v\), the continuous representatives \(e_P,m_{0,P},m_{1,P}\) exist uniquely and are independent of the chosen conditional kernel versions. For \(x,z\in[0,1]\), \(|m_{1,P}(x)-m_{1,P}(z)|\le40|x-z|^{\min\{\beta,\gamma\}}\). The completion \(\mathbb Q_P\) has observed marginal \(P\), satisfies \((Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid X\), and has conditional causal mean effect equal to \(\tau_P\) \(\lambda\)-almost everywhere; its unique continuous representative is \(\tau_P\). Also \(d(P)=0\) if and only if \(P\in H_0(v)\), and \(d_0\le D_v\le1/2\). A legal separated witness is \(e_P(x)=1/2+\sin(2\pi x)/10\), \(m_{0,P}(x)=\cos(2\pi x)/8\), \(\tau_P(x)=\cos(2\pi x)/8\), with deterministic conditional outcomes; replacing only \(\tau_P\) by \(1/8\) gives a legal nonzero-constant null.

items.label: Lemma L-2
items.nl:
For \(n\ge4\) use Definition \(\mathrm{def:explicit\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}ledger}\), and put \(e_K=\Pi_K e_P\) and \(w_K=e_P(1-e_K)\). The mean \(\theta_P(c)=E_PZ_b(c)\) satisfies, for every \(|c|\le1/2\),
\[
 \left\|\theta_P(c)-\int_0^1 F_M(x)w_K(x)(\tau_P(x)-c)\,dx\right\|_2\le B,
 \qquad
 \|\theta_P(c)\|_2\ge\frac3{16}d(P)-16M^{-\gamma}-B.
\]
If \(P\in H_0(v)\) with effect \(c_0\), then \(\|\theta_P(c_0)\|_2\le B\). These bounds require no regularity of clipped conditional means.

items.label: Lemma L-3
items.nl:
Write the explicit score as \(Z_b(c)=Z_{b,0}-cZ_{b,A}\). For every \(P\in\mathcal M_v\), both coefficients are square integrable and
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P(Z_{b,0})\preceq\Lambda_{n,v}I_M,
 \qquad \operatorname{Cov}_P(Z_{b,A})\preceq\Lambda_{n,v}I_M.
\]
In particular \(|u^T\operatorname{Cov}_P(Z_{b,0},Z_{b,A})z|\le\Lambda_{n,v}\|u\|_2\|z\|_2\). These bounds include every cross-level covariance and hold without any bound on \(K/n\).

items.label: Lemma L-4
items.nl:
For the explicit score construction and every \(P\in\mathcal M_v\), with probability at least \(0.9925\), simultaneously for every \(c\in[-1/2,1/2]\),
\[
 |W(c)-\|\theta_P(c)\|_2^2|
 \le128\{\sqrt{\Lambda_{n,v}}\|\theta_P(c)\|_2
                   +\sqrt{J_{\mathrm c}}\Lambda_{n,v}\}.
\]
When the right-hand side is zero the error is zero almost surely and the corresponding ratio is assigned value zero.

items.label: Lemma L-5
items.nl:
For every \(v\in\mathcal V\), put \(q=(p-1)/p\), \(E_0=2\gamma q/(2\gamma+q)\), and
\(c^{\mathrm e}_v=4^{-\gamma}/(16\sqrt3)\). For every \(n\ge2\) there is a legal null law and a finite mixture of legal alternatives, all with the same entire propensity \(e_P\equiv1/2\), such that every alternative has
\[
 c^{\mathrm e}_vn^{-E_0}\le d(P)<d_0\le D_v,
 \qquad \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},\overline P_1^{(n)})<1/2.
\]
Each arm outcome law is concentrated on \(\{0,-L,L\}\); positive mass at every displayed atom is not required. Here \(L\to\infty\), and the raw conditional \(p\)-moment is at most one. Consequently
\[
 B_n^{\mathrm e}(v,c^{\mathrm e}_vn^{-E_0})\ge2/5>1/10,
 \qquad B_n(v,c^{\mathrm e}_vn^{-E_0})\ge2/5.
\]
For every valid bounded tuple \(w=(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in\mathcal W\) and every \(n\ge2\), a separate signed-binary construction supplies a legal signed-binary null \(P_0^{\mathrm b}\in H_0^{\mathrm{bin}}(w)\) and a normalized nonempty finite probability prior \(\pi_1^{\mathrm b}\) supported on legal signed-binary alternatives in \(\mathcal M_w^{\mathrm{bin}}\). The entire propensity of the null and every alternative is \(e_P\equiv1/2\). With \(c^{\mathrm b}_w=4^{-\gamma}/(16\sqrt3)\), every alternative in the positive-weight support satisfies
\[
 c^{\mathrm b}_w n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+1)}\le d(P)<d_0\le D_w^{\mathrm b}.
\]
Writing \(\overline P_{1,\mathrm b}^{(n)}=\int P^{\otimes n}\,\pi_1^{\mathrm b}(dP)\) for its full original-record mixture, the same witnesses satisfy
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\bigl((P_0^{\mathrm b})^{\otimes n},\overline P_{1,\mathrm b}^{(n)}\bigr)<1/2,
 \qquad B_n^{\mathrm b}\bigl(w,c^{\mathrm b}_w n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+1)}\bigr)\ge2/5.
\]
All these alternatives are nonempty for every \(n\ge2\).

items.label: Lemma L-6
items.nl:
Put \(q=(p-1)/p\), \(S=\alpha+\beta\), and \(F(p)=2\alpha/(p-1)+\beta/q+S/(2\gamma)\). Suppose \(F(p)<1\). For dyadic \(K\ge16M\), \(M\ge2\), \(M\le K^{S/\gamma}\), use Definition \(\mathrm{def:copula\mbox{-}frame\mbox{-}priors}\) with
\[
 a=K^{-\alpha}/16,\quad b=K^{-\beta}/256,\quad
 u=1/16,\quad\varepsilon=(16b)^{1/q},\quad L=\varepsilon^{-1/p}.
\]
Every support law of \(\pi_0\) belongs to \(H_0(v)\); every support law of \(\pi_1\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_v\) and has deterministic, centered effect
\[
 \tau_P=-\frac{2ab\kappa}{1-a^2}\widetilde g_\sigma,\qquad
 2^{-17}K^{-S}\le d(P)\le2^{-14}K^{-S}<d_0.
\]
Every conditional arm raw \(p\)-moment equals one. For the bounded version take \(v=(2,w)\), \(F(2)<1\), keep \(a,b\), and instead use \(u=2b\), \(\varepsilon=1/2\), \(L=1\). Its supports are bounded nulls and bounded alternatives with exactly the same effect and distance bounds. Its conditional arm raw second moment is \(1/2\).

items.label: Lemma L-7
items.nl:
For the priors of Definition \(\mathrm{def:copula\mbox{-}frame\mbox{-}priors}\), suppose \(K\ge2^{40}n\), \(K\ge16M\), \(M\ge2\), and \(0<a,u\le1/16\). There is a common-design augmentation and a normalized intermediate probability law \(Q\) such that, conditional on the common design and disclosure, \(\chi^2(Q\Vert P_0)\le\exp(\mathcal A)-1\) and \(\chi^2(P_1\Vert Q)\le\exp(\mathcal B)-1\), where
\[
 E\mathcal A\le2^{38}a^4u^4\varepsilon^2 n^2/K,\qquad
 E\mathcal B\le2^{56}a^4u^4\varepsilon^2 n^4/(MK^2).
\]
The expectations include every occupancy and all six record categories. In particular, if the sum of these two displayed upper bounds is at most \(2^{-16}\), then
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\left(\int P^{\otimes n}\pi_0(dP),
                         \int P^{\otimes n}\pi_1(dP)\right)<1/8.
\]
No transition tensor is assumed zero, and no coarse sign is disclosed.

Here the existing common augmentation conditioning coordinate is precisely the triple
\[
 \left((X_i)_{i=1}^n,(B_i)_{i=1}^n,\mathcal D_{\partial}\right),
 \qquad B_i=\mathbf1\{Y_i\ne0\},
\]
where \(\mathcal D_{\partial}\) discloses exactly the coefficient pairs \((\lambda_j,\eta_j)\) at the boundary nodes \(j/K=k/M\), \(0\le k\le M\), and no coarse sign. Under both mixtures, the covariates are iid \(\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), the flags are iid \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\varepsilon)\), and the covariates, flags and boundary disclosure are mutually independent. The disclosed boundary coefficient pairs are independent fair pairs with the same law under both priors and are independent of all coarse signs. Both displayed conditional chi-square inequalities are conditional on this full triple; the expectations of \(\mathcal A\) and \(\mathcal B\) integrate its common law.

items.label: Lemma L-8
items.nl:
Use Definition \(\mathrm{def:sharp\mbox{-}frontier\mbox{-}scales}\). If \(F(p)<1\), then for every \(n\ge2\) there are finite null and alternative mixtures on the entire original class such that
\[
 c_v n^{-E_4(p)}\le d(P)<d_0\le D_v
 \quad\text{on every alternative support law},\qquad
 \operatorname{TV}(\mathbb P_0,\mathbb P_1)<1/2,
 \qquad B_n(v,c_vn^{-E_4(p)})\ge2/5.
\]
For \(n\ge N_{\mathrm{low}}(v)\), take \(K\) to be the least power of two at least \(H_{\mathrm{fine}}n^{2/D_p}\), and
\[
 M=2^{\lfloor\log_2(K^{S/\gamma}/16)\rfloor}.
\]
Use the tail tuning of Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:copula\mbox{-}frame\mbox{-}legality}\). These mixtures have total variation below \(1/8\). For \(n<N_{\mathrm{low}}(v)\), use the established paired-tent mixtures. At \(p=2\), the same tuning of ranks with the separate bounded version of that legality lemma proves
\[
 B_n^{\mathrm b}(w,c_w^{\mathrm b}n^{-E_4(2)})\ge2/5
 \quad\text{whenever }F(2)<1,
\]
with legal nonempty bounded alternatives for every \(n\).

items.label: Theorem T-1
items.nl: For every \(v=(p,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in\mathcal V\), with \(w=(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\), \[\mathcal M^{\mathrm{bin}}_w\subseteq\mathcal M^{\mathrm b}_w\subseteq\mathcal M_v,\qquad D_w^{\mathrm{bin}}=D_w^{\mathrm b}=D_v\ge d_0.\] For every \(n\ge2\) and \(0<r<D_v\), \[B_n^{\mathrm{bin}}(w,r)=B_n^{\mathrm b}(w,r)\le B_n(v,r),\qquad 0<r_n^{*,\mathrm{bin}}(w)=r_n^{*,\mathrm b}(w)\le r_n^*(v).\] A bounded record can be converted to a signed-binary record by keeping \((X,A)\) and drawing a sign with conditional mean \(Y\); this preserves both arm means, the propensity and \(d(P)\). Every permissible primitive mean triple has a signed-binary realization. Independent conversion randomization is integrated into a Borel rejection probability based on the original records and public randomization.

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl: Determine when an armwise conditional \(p\)-moment envelope strictly enlarges the full-record critical radius for constancy of the original mean CATE relative to the corresponding bounded and signed-binary models. For every \(v\in\mathcal V\), with \(w=(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\), derive explicit evaluable \(\rho_n(v)>0\) and \(\rho_n^{\mathrm b}(w)>0\) tending to zero, with every power, necessary logarithm, phase and saturation computed from matched upper and lower bounds. For every \(n\ge2\), establish \[c_v\rho_n(v)\le r_n^*(v)\le C_v\rho_n(v),\qquad c_w^{\mathrm b}\rho_n^{\mathrm b}(w)\le r_n^{*,\mathrm b}(w)=r_n^{*,\mathrm{bin}}(w)\le C_w^{\mathrm b}\rho_n^{\mathrm b}(w),\] with positive lower and finite upper constants locally uniform on compact exponent sets, including all equality regimes. Determine \(\mathcal T\) and \(\mathcal E\) by explicit inequalities in \((p,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\), prove that \(\mathcal T\) contains a nonempty relatively open subset with \(1<p<2\), and compute the order of \(\Delta_n(v)\) throughout the domain. Identify every equality and transition regime, including whether the bounded rough-confounding branch remains rate-determining outside the strict region and any additional boundary behavior. On \(\mathcal T\), the matched finite-moment scale must asymptotically exceed the matched bounded scale and its converse must be tail-essential in the following full-record sense: the legal finite null and alternative priors use marks \(L_{n,v}\to\infty\), while for every fixed \(p<2\) and all sufficiently large \(n\) there do not exist normalized finite priors supported respectively on \(H_0^{\mathrm b}(w)\) and \(\{P\in\mathcal M_w^{\mathrm b}:c_v\rho_n(v)\le d(P)\}\) whose complete-record mixture total variation is below \(1/2\), as proved in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:tail\mbox{-}essential\mbox{-}full\mbox{-}record\mbox{-}converse}\). Construct total observable original-record rules \(\phi^*_{n,v}\) and \(\phi^{*,\mathrm b}_{n,w}\) with exactly finite-sample size bounds \[\sup_{P\in H_0(v)}\mathsf R_n(P,\phi^*_{n,v})\le1/10,\qquad \sup_{P\in H_0^{\mathrm b}(w)}\mathsf R_n(P,\phi^{*,\mathrm b}_{n,w})\le1/10.\] Their worst-case type-II errors are at most \(1/10\) over their respective classes at separations \(C_v\rho_n(v)\) and \(C_w^{\mathrm b}\rho_n^{\mathrm b}(w)\), whenever these are strictly below \(D_v\) and \(D_w^{\mathrm b}\). Give public finite \(N_v,N_w^{\mathrm b}\) after which the corresponding separations are below \(d_0\); before those thresholds report total size-valid calibration or fallback without empty-alternative power. For every \(n\ge2\), require \(0<c_v\rho_n(v)<D_v\) and \(0<c_w^{\mathrm b}\rho_n^{\mathrm b}(w)<D_w^{\mathrm b}\), and prove \[B_n(v,c_v\rho_n(v))>1/10,\qquad B_n^{\mathrm b}(w,c_w^{\mathrm b}\rho_n^{\mathrm b}(w))>1/10\] using legal nonempty alternatives against all original-record randomized tests. Specify all ranks, cutoffs, rounding, missing-cell and small-sample branches as finite public computations. No propensity function is supplied in either headline experiment.

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl:
Use the total ranks, separate cutoffs, bias ledger \(\mathfrak b_{n,v}\), covariance ledger \(\Lambda_{n,v}\), and cutoff \(h_{n,v}\) of Definition \(\mathrm{def:explicit\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}ledger}\). For every \(n\ge2\) and every \(P\in\mathcal M_v\), both centered affine coefficients have covariance at most \(\Lambda_{n,v}I_{J_{\mathrm c}}\). The simultaneous ratio in the source question is at most \(C=128\) with probability at least \(0.9925\), using zero for an identically zero numerator and denominator. Under \(P\in H_0(v)\), \(\inf_c\|\theta_P(c)\|_2\le\mathfrak b_{n,v}\). The original-record rule \(\psi_{n,v}\) of that definition has exactly finite-sample size at most \(0.0075<1/10\). For \(n\ge4\), its type-II error is at most \(0.0075\) uniformly over the nonempty alternative whenever
\[
 d(P)\ge R_{\mathrm{att}}(n,v)
 :=\frac{16}{3}\left\{16J_{\mathrm c}^{-\gamma}
       +5\mathfrak b_{n,v}
       +1024J_{\mathrm c}^{1/4}\sqrt{\Lambda_{n,v}}\right\}.
\]
A power claim is made only if its displayed separation is strictly below \(D_v\). The test is zero for \(n=2,3\). All covariance and profiling assertions include cross-level and cross-coefficient covariances and all two-, three-, and four-record contractions, without requiring \(J_{\mathrm f}\le n\).

items.label: Theorem T-4
items.nl:
The supplied-propensity frontier is resolved independently of the unknown-propensity rough converse. For every public tuple let
\[
 q=(p-1)/p,\quad E_0=2\gamma q/(2\gamma+q),\quad
 \rho_n^{\mathrm e}(v)=n^{-E_0},\quad
 c^{\mathrm e}_v=4^{-\gamma}/(16\sqrt3),\quad
 C^{\mathrm e}_v=3\{120+128\sqrt{160\sqrt2}\}.
\]
For every \(n\ge2\),
\[
 c^{\mathrm e}_v\rho_n^{\mathrm e}(v)\le r_n^{*,\mathrm e}(v)
                      \le C^{\mathrm e}_v\rho_n^{\mathrm e}(v).
\]
Here is a total attaining rule. Put \(s=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), \(a=s^{-E_0}\), \(T=2^{\lceil\log_2(a^{-1/(p-1)})\rceil}\), and let \(J\) be the least power of two at least \(a^{-1/\gamma}\). Put \(u=J^{-1/2}(1,\ldots,1)^T\), \(C_J=I_J-uu^T\), and
\[
 R_i=\frac{A_i\ell_T(Y_i)}{e_P(X_i)}
       -\frac{(1-A_i)\ell_T(Y_i)}{1-e_P(X_i)},\quad
 V_b=s^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_b}C_JF_J(X_i)R_i.
\]
Set \(b=20T^{1-p}\), \(\Lambda=80T^{2-p}/s\), and reject when
\(\langle V_1,V_2\rangle>2b^2+1024\sqrt J\Lambda\).
Extend this Borel map to a supplied continuous function outside \([1/4,3/4]\) by first clipping it into that interval. This rule is \(\phi^{*,\mathrm e}_{n,v}\). Its size is at most \(0.01\) on the entire unknown-constant original-mean null, and its type-II error is at most \(0.01\) at the displayed separation whenever that separation is below \(D_v\). A public nonempty-power threshold is
\[
 N^{\mathrm e}_v=\left\lceil\max\{2,(2C^{\mathrm e}_v/d_0)^{1/E_0}\}\right\rceil.
\]
Before that threshold the finite rule remains calibrated; a level at or above \(D_v\) records only saturation. The converse has nonempty alternatives and identical entire supplied propensity for every \(n\). Constants are locally uniform including \(p=2\) and \(\gamma=1/4\). No logarithm is necessary.

items.label: Theorem T-5
items.nl:
For every public tuple define
\[
 q=(p-1)/p,\quad S=\alpha+\beta,\quad t=(2-p)/(p-1),\quad
 E_0=2\gamma q/(2\gamma+q),\quad
 E_4=\frac{2S}{1+2\alpha+\beta/q+S/(2\gamma)},\quad E=\min\{E_0,E_4\}.
\]
The explicit original-record rule in Definition \(\mathrm{def:explicit\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}ledger}\) attains separation at most \(C^{\mathrm{att}}_v n^{-E}\), with exactly finite-sample size and type-II error at most \(0.0075\), the latter whenever \(C^{\mathrm{att}}_v n^{-E}<D_v\). A fully evaluable choice is the following. Put \(s_0=\min\{\alpha,\beta,\gamma\}\), \(\lambda_0=(p-1)^2/(4p)\), \(\eta_0=(p-1)(p+6)/(4p)\), and \(A(x)=(1-2^{-x})^{-1}\) for \(x>0\). Define
\[
 \begin{split}
 B_*&=420+800\{A(\alpha)+A(\lambda_0)\},\\
 D_*&=1+\{\exp(1)S\log2\}^{-1},\\
 L_*&=16+880A(s_0)+160D_*+960A(\alpha),\\
 G_*&=\sqrt{64}\{2^{t/2}A(1/2)+A(\eta_0/2)\},\\
 A_*&=\sqrt2\{24576+64L_*^2+16384+256G_*^2\},\\
 C^{\mathrm{att}}_v&=16\{16+5B_*+1024\sqrt{A_*}\},\\
 N^{\mathrm{att}}_v&=\left\lceil\max\{4,(2C^{\mathrm{att}}_v/d_0)^{1/E}\}\right\rceil.
 \end{split}
\]
Then \(r_n^*(v)\le C^{\mathrm{att}}_vn^{-E}\) for every \(n\ge2\), and the displayed power level is below \(d_0\) for every \(n\ge N^{\mathrm{att}}_v\). These public constants are locally bounded on compact subsets of the entire exponent domain, including equality regimes. No logarithm in \(n\) is present in this attainable rate. For \(n<N^{\mathrm{att}}_v\) the same rule remains size valid, with its zero branch at \(n=2,3\); a level at or above \(D_v\) gives only the capped upper comparison, not empty-alternative power. Applying the same rule with \(p=2\) to the bounded model gives the corresponding attainable bounded exponent
\[
 E_{\mathrm b}=\min\left\{\frac{2\gamma}{4\gamma+1},
                         \frac{2S}{1+2S+S/(2\gamma)}\right\}.
\]

items.label: Theorem T-6
items.nl:
Use the explicit scales and constants of Definition \(\mathrm{def:sharp\mbox{-}frontier\mbox{-}scales}\). For every \(v\in\mathcal V\) and every \(n\ge2\), there are the following explicit finite mixing laws and rare-mark parameters satisfying
\[
 \pi_{0,n,v}(H_0(v))=1,\quad
 \pi_{1,n,v}\{P\in\mathcal M_v:c_v\rho_n(v)\le d(P)<D_v\}=1,
 \quad0<c_v\rho_n(v)<D_v,
\]
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(\mathbb P_{0,n,v},\mathbb P_{1,n,v})<1/2,
 \qquad B_n(v,c_v\rho_n(v))\ge2/5>1/10.
\]
When \(F(p)<1\) and \(n\ge N_{\mathrm{low}}(v)\), use the dyadic \(K,M\) and tail copula priors of Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:rough\mbox{-}full\mbox{-}record\mbox{-}sharp\mbox{-}lower}\), with
\[
 \varepsilon_{n,v}=16^{-1/q}K^{-\beta/q},\qquad
 L_{n,v}=\varepsilon_{n,v}^{-1/p}.
\]
Otherwise use the established opposite paired-tent family, with
\[
 N=2\lceil n^{2q/(2\gamma+q)}\rceil,\quad h=1/N,\quad
 \varepsilon_{n,v}=h^{\gamma/q},\qquad L_{n,v}=h^{-\gamma/(p-1)}.
\]
All arm supports are contained in \(\{0,-L_{n,v},L_{n,v}\}\), all support laws satisfy every original primitive predicate separately, and \(L_{n,v}\to\infty\). Every alternative has a deterministic \(\gamma\)-smooth original mean effect conditional on its latent coefficients. The complete-record likelihood bound retains zero marks, both treatment labels, all occupancies, and the odd overlap tensors. Throughout \(p<2\), \(\rho_n(v)/\rho_n^{\mathrm b}(w)\to\infty\). A normalized finite prior means a probability measure \(\pi=\sum_{j=1}^{k}\omega_j\delta_{P_j}\) on original-record laws, with \(k\ge1\), \(\omega_j\ge0\) and \(\sum_j\omega_j=1\). Its positive-weight support is \(\operatorname{supp}_+(\pi)=\{P_j:\omega_j>0\}\), and its complete-record mixture is
\[
 \mathbb P_{\pi,n}=\int P^{\otimes n}\,\pi(dP).
\]
Write \(w=(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\). For each fixed \(v\in\mathcal V\) with \(p<2\), there exists an integer \(N(v)\ge2\) such that for every \(n\ge N(v)\) and every pair of normalized finite priors \(\pi_0,\pi_1\),
\[
 \left.
 \begin{gathered}
  \operatorname{supp}_+(\pi_0)\subseteq H_0^{\mathrm b}(w),\\
  \operatorname{supp}_+(\pi_1)\subseteq
      \{P\in\mathcal M_w^{\mathrm b}:c_v\rho_n(v)\le d(P)\}
 \end{gathered}
 \right\}
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{TV}(\mathbb P_{\pi_0,n},\mathbb P_{\pi_1,n})\ge\frac12.
\]
Thus the exclusion quantifies over all such finite prior pairs, separately for each fixed tuple.

On the complementary face \(p=2\), for every \(n\ge2\), take the branchwise bounded witness pair \(\pi^{\mathrm b}_{0,n,v},\pi^{\mathrm b}_{1,n,v}\): use the signed-binary paired-tent package when \(F(2)\ge1\), the bounded rough package when \(F(2)<1\) and \(n\ge N_{\mathrm{low}}(v)\), and the signed-binary paired-tent fallback otherwise. Both priors are normalized finite probability laws with nonempty positive-weight supports. Define \(\mathbb P^{\mathrm b}_{\nu,n,v}=\mathbb P_{\pi^{\mathrm b}_{\nu,n,v},n}\), \(\nu\in\{0,1\}\). They satisfy
\[
 \begin{gathered}
  \sum_{P\in\operatorname{supp}_+(\pi^{\mathrm b}_{\nu,n,v})}
       \pi^{\mathrm b}_{\nu,n,v}(\{P\})=1,\qquad \nu\in\{0,1\},\\
  \operatorname{supp}_+(\pi^{\mathrm b}_{0,n,v})\subseteq H_0^{\mathrm b}(w),\\
  \operatorname{supp}_+(\pi^{\mathrm b}_{1,n,v})\subseteq
     \{P\in\mathcal M_w^{\mathrm b}:c_v\rho_n(v)\le d(P)<d_0\},\\
  \operatorname{TV}(\mathbb P^{\mathrm b}_{0,n,v},
                    \mathbb P^{\mathrm b}_{1,n,v})<\frac12,\\
  \frac25\le B_n^{\mathrm b}(w,c_v\rho_n(v))
          \le B_n(v,c_v\rho_n(v)).
 \end{gathered}
\]
The unchanged scales and multipliers agree on this face:
\[
 \rho_n(v)=\rho_n^{\mathrm b}(w),\qquad
 c_v=c_w^{\mathrm b},\qquad C_v=C_w^{\mathrm b}.
\]
The bounded lower witnesses and the established original-record attainable theorem therefore give, for every \(n\ge2\),
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 c_v\rho_n(v)\le r_n^*(v)\le C_v\rho_n(v),\\
 c_w^{\mathrm b}\rho_n^{\mathrm b}(w)
 \le r_n^{*,\mathrm b}(w)=r_n^{*,\mathrm{bin}}(w)
 \le C_w^{\mathrm b}\rho_n^{\mathrm b}(w).
 \end{gathered}
\]
The upper inequalities use the existing total original and bounded rules and retain their finite-sample conditions:
\[
 \sup_{P\in H_0(v)}\mathsf R_n(P,\phi^*_{n,v})\le0.0075,
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in H_0^{\mathrm b}(w)}
      \mathsf R_n(P,\phi^{*,\mathrm b}_{n,w})\le0.0075.
\]
Only when \(C_v\rho_n(v)<D_v=D_w^{\mathrm b}\), the alternatives are nonempty and
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_v:\ d(P)\ge C_v\rho_n(v)}
     \{1-\mathsf R_n(P,\phi^*_{n,v})\}\le0.0075,\\
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_w^{\mathrm b}:\ d(P)\ge
                        C_w^{\mathrm b}\rho_n^{\mathrm b}(w)}
     \{1-\mathsf R_n(P,\phi^{*,\mathrm b}_{n,w})\}\le0.0075.
 \end{gathered}
\]
The existing public thresholds satisfy \(N_v=N_w^{\mathrm b}\) on \(p=2\), and for \(n\ge N_v\) the common power separation is at most \(d_0/2\), hence strictly below both maxima. Before that threshold the rules remain calibrated, with their zero branch at \(n=2,3\); a nominal level at or above the common maximum asserts only saturation. All constructions, constants and conclusions are the existing ones assembled on this face.

items.label: Theorem T-7
items.nl:
For \(v=(p,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in\mathcal V\), define
\[
 q=\frac{p-1}{p},\qquad S=\alpha+\beta,\qquad
 D_p=1+2\alpha+\frac\beta q+\frac S{2\gamma},
\]
\[
 E_0(p)=\frac{2\gamma q}{2\gamma+q},\qquad
 E_4(p)=\frac{2S}{D_p},\qquad
 F(p)=\frac{2\alpha}{p-1}+\frac\beta q+\frac S{2\gamma},
\]
\[
 G(v)=\max\{0,E_0(p)-E_4(p)\}
     =\frac{2\gamma q}{(2\gamma+q)D_p}\max\{0,1-F(p)\}.
\]
Keep the unchanged multipliers \(c_v,C_v\) of Definition
\(\mathrm{def:sharp\mbox{-}frontier\mbox{-}scales}\), and put
\[
 c^{\mathrm e}_v=\frac{4^{-\gamma}}{16\sqrt3},\qquad
 C^{\mathrm e}_v=3\{120+128\sqrt{160\sqrt2}\}.
\]
For the unknown- and supplied-propensity experiments on the same entire class
\(\mathcal M_v\), for every \(n\ge2\),
\[
 \frac{c_v}{C^{\mathrm e}_v}n^{G(v)}
 \le \frac{r_n^*(v)}{r_n^{*,\mathrm e}(v)}
 \le \frac{C_v}{c^{\mathrm e}_v}n^{G(v)}.
\]
Consequently the exact preservation region is
\[
 \mathcal R=
 \left\{v\in\mathcal V:
 \frac{2\alpha}{p-1}+\frac\beta q+
 \frac{\alpha+\beta}{2\gamma}\ge1\right\}.
\]
At every equality point \(F(p)=1\), the ratio is bounded above and below
by positive constants independent of \(n\), with no necessary logarithmic
factor. If \(F(p)<1\), then
\[
 \frac{r_n^*(v)}{r_n^{*,\mathrm e}(v)}
 \asymp_v n^{E_0(p)-E_4(p)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The displayed comparison constants are locally uniform on every compact
subset of \(\mathcal V\), including compact sets crossing \(F(p)=1\)
and touching \(p=2\) or \(\gamma=1/4\). These are comparisons of capped
critical radii for every sample size; they do not assert power at an empty
alternative in a saturated small-sample regime. The boundary is a corollary
of the two established matched frontiers, rather than a new identifying
functional or an estimator-rate condition.

items.label: Theorem T-8
items.nl:
The primary supplied-propensity result holds on the broader continuous-carrier class \(\mathcal M_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}\), which deletes only the quantitative \(\alpha\)-H\"older propensity and \(\beta\)-H\"older baseline restrictions. For every public \(v=(p,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in\mathcal V\), put
\[
 q=\frac{p-1}{p},\qquad E_0=\frac{2\gamma q}{2\gamma+q},\qquad
 \rho_n^{\mathrm e}(v)=n^{-E_0},\qquad
 c_v^{\mathrm e}=\frac{4^{-\gamma}}{16\sqrt3},\qquad
 C_v^{\mathrm e}=3\{120+128\sqrt{160\sqrt2}\}.
\]
The broader maximum satisfies \(d_0\le D_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}\le1/2\), and for every \(n\ge2\),
\[
 c_v^{\mathrm e}\rho_n^{\mathrm e}(v)
 \le r_n^{*,\mathrm{e,br}}(v)
 \le C_v^{\mathrm e}\rho_n^{\mathrm e}(v),\qquad
 B_n^{\mathrm{e,br}}(v,c_v^{\mathrm e}\rho_n^{\mathrm e}(v))\ge2/5.
\]
The attaining map is exactly the existing \(\phi^{*,\mathrm e}_{n,v}\), with the same supplied continuous propensity and the same original records and public randomization. Explicitly, put \(s=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), \(a=s^{-E_0}\),
\[
 T=2^{\lceil\log_2(a^{-1/(p-1)})\rceil},\qquad
 J=2^{\lceil\log_2(a^{-1/\gamma})\rceil},\qquad
 u=J^{-1/2}(1,\ldots,1)^T,\qquad C_J=I_J-uu^T.
\]
For any supplied \(f\in C([0,1])\), put \(\widetilde f(x)=\max\{1/4,\min\{f(x),3/4\}\}\) and form
\[
 R_i(f)=\frac{A_i\ell_T(Y_i)}{\widetilde f(X_i)}
       -\frac{(1-A_i)\ell_T(Y_i)}{1-\widetilde f(X_i)},\qquad
 V_b(f)=s^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_b}C_JF_J(X_i)R_i(f),
 \quad b\in\{1,2\}.
\]
With \(b_T=20T^{1-p}\) and \(\Lambda=80T^{2-p}/s\), reject exactly when
\[
 \langle V_1(f),V_2(f)\rangle>2b_T^2+1024\sqrt J\Lambda.
\]
This is a total jointly Borel map; it may ignore the independent public seed. At the true supply \(f=e_P\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in H_0^{\mathrm{e,br}}(v)}
     \mathsf R_n^{\mathrm e}(P,\phi^{*,\mathrm e}_{n,v})\le0.01.
\]
If \(C_v^{\mathrm e}\rho_n^{\mathrm e}(v)<D_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}\), the alternative is nonempty and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}:\,
              d(P)\ge C_v^{\mathrm e}\rho_n^{\mathrm e}(v)}
   \{1-\mathsf R_n^{\mathrm e}(P,\phi^{*,\mathrm e}_{n,v})\}\le0.01.
\]
A public nonempty-power threshold, with the identical formula and constants, is
\[
 N_v^{\mathrm e}=\left\lceil
       \max\{2,(2C_v^{\mathrm e}/d_0)^{1/E_0}\}\right\rceil.
\]
For \(n\ge N_v^{\mathrm e}\), the attaining separation is at most \(d_0/2<D_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}\). Before this threshold the finite rule remains calibrated; a separation at or above \(D_v^{\mathrm{e,br}}\) asserts only saturation.

The converse uses the established legal null and normalized nonempty finite alternative mixture of Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:paired\mbox{-}tent\mbox{-}full\mbox{-}record\mbox{-}lower}\). These laws enter the broader classes by inclusion. Their entire propensity is the same function \(e_P\equiv1/2\); every alternative has \(c_v^{\mathrm e}n^{-E_0}\le d(P)<d_0\), and their full original-record mixture total variation is below \(1/2\). Thus necessity holds against every allowed original-record randomized supplied-propensity test. All remaining model conditions, the original causal mean target, constants, tuning, calibration, power and lower witnesses are unchanged. The upper proof consumes neither deleted H\"older condition. Constants and the exponent are locally uniform on compact subsets of \(\mathcal V\), including \(p=2\), \(\gamma=1/4\), and equality regimes in the same-class comparison; no logarithmic factor is necessary. The unchanged Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:oracle\mbox{-}frontier\mbox{-}resolved}\) remains the same-class compatibility input to Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:exact\mbox{-}propensity\mbox{-}preservation\mbox{-}boundary}\).
